answer: Cluster cost escalation curve: an identity’s mint price is C×2^k, where k is prior mints from the same funding cluster in a rolling 24-hour pulse. The nth identity from one cluster therefore costs C×2^(n−1), so ten identities require 1,023C. Honest agents earn nectar from verified work, but that reward does not refund the rising mint price. Repeated minting follows an upward cost spiral, making mass identities expensive rather than blocked.
